record.paper_title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism. Maxent-Nesom: Concepts, Construction, Application, Open Questions and Criticisms
record.original_question: For many-body systems away from equilibrium, can one construct a Gibbs-style statistical ensemble formalism analogous to the standard equilibrium ensembles, and if so, what are the correct nonequilibrium ensembles for deriving irreversible thermodynamics, thermo-hydrodynamics, nonlinear kinetic theory, response functions, transport coefficients, and the time evolution of macroscopic observables?

evidence.quote: What are the right ensembles for nonequilibrium problems?
The last item (e) is connected with Penrose's question noticed in the Introduction concerning if there are, and what are, right ensembles for nonequilibrium problems.

In the preceding sections we have described, in terms of a general overview, a theory that attempts a particular answer to the long-standing sought-after question about the existence of a Gibbs-style statistical ensemble formalism for nonequilibrium systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a classical or quantum many-body system with Hamiltonian H acting on a phase space (or Hilbert space) Γ, whose microscopic dynamics is generated by the Liouville (or von Neumann) equation for a statistical distribution ρ(t). In equilibrium statistical mechanics, Gibbs ensembles (microcanonical, canonical, grand canonical) are defined as distributions ρ_eq that maximize the Gibbs–Shannon entropy S[ρ] = −Tr(ρ ln ρ) subject to constraints fixing the conserved quantities (energy, particle number, etc.), and from them one derives equilibrium thermodynamics, response functions, and fluctuation formulas.

The problem is to construct an analogous Gibbs-style statistical ensemble formalism valid for many-body systems arbitrarily far from equilibrium. Specifically:

1. Identify a class of nonequilibrium statistical operators ρ(t) on Γ, parameterized by a set of macroscopic observables {P_j(t)} (informational basis), such that ρ(t) is determined by an extremum principle (e.g. maximization of an information-theoretic entropy S[ρ] = −Tr(ρ ln ρ) under the constraints Tr[ρ(t) P_j] = ⟨P_j⟩(t) together with appropriate retroeffect / initial-condition conditions encoding irreversibility).

2. Show that the resulting ensembles are compatible with the underlying microscopic Liouville (or von Neumann) evolution, in the sense that the evolution equations for ⟨P_j⟩(t) are derivable from the microdynamics.

3. From this ensemble, systematically derive: (i) the laws of irreversible thermodynamics (entropy production, H-theorem); (ii) closed thermo-hydrodynamic equations for the relevant macrovariables; (iii) a nonlinear kinetic theory for the one-particle distribution function; (iv) generalized response functions and fluctuation–dissipation relations valid out of equilibrium; (v) explicit expressions for transport coefficients.

4. Characterize the correct choice of informational basis {P_j} and provide criteria under which the resulting ensemble is unique and uniquely encodes the irreversible macroscopic behavior of the system.

The overall question is whether such a Gibbs-style nonequilibrium ensemble formalism exists with the same logical status, generality, and predictive completeness as the equilibrium Gibbs ensembles, and if so to specify it explicitly.
artifact.status_search_result: The construction of a fully satisfactory Gibbs-style ensemble theory for arbitrary nonequilibrium systems remains a long-standing open foundational problem in statistical mechanics. Several partial frameworks exist (Zubanev's NSO/MaxEnt-NESOM, Mori–Zwanzig projection operators, GENERIC, steady-state thermodynamics, large-deviation approaches, and recent stochastic thermodynamics), but none is universally accepted as the definitive analog of equilibrium Gibbs ensembles, and the question—often attributed to Oliver Penrose—is still discussed as open in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Penrose, Foundations of statistical mechanics
status_evidence.snippet: There is no general statistical mechanics framework for systems far from equilibrium analogous to the Gibbs ensembles.
status_evidence.claim: The general nonequilibrium ensemble problem is widely regarded as unresolved.
